messages:
olivia: Heads up — seeing a cluster-wide spike in GPU attach timeouts in us-west2 starting ~02:00 UTC. About ~15% of pod launches errored with AttachTimeout and mount failures. Also seeing local-ssd IO spikes on the same hosts.

mike: Pasted iostat from one host around 02:04: 
```
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           6.12    0.00    8.23   70.45    0.00   15.20
Device             r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz   await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00  540.00   48.00 21600.00   78.00    9.65   18.90   1.20  19.70  0.12  99.90
```
Looks like continuous high write util, avgqu-sz ~9.6. fstrim backlog also piled up.

sara: FYI we rolled a network config (BGP peer tweak + MTU change) to half the racks at 01:58 UTC. Did that change un-pin scratchpool affinity or trigger reassigns?

kai: Confirmed — netcfg rollout changed node labels via the automation (we accidentally removed `scratch-affinity` label from ~240 nodes for a short window). Our rebalancer saw nodes as eligible and kicked a global janitor reassign. That caused many scrub/cleanup jobs to start roughly at the same time. :exclamation:

janitor-bot: Automated alert: started scrub workload on 240 nodes at 02:03:12 UTC due to node-label change. Concurrency target: 100 jobs -> escalated to global scheduler. Reason: detected lost scratch-affinity label.

mike: Correlation matrix: scrub start -> nvme write amps spike -> provisioners time out. smartctl on affected device: 
```
smartctl -A /dev/nvme0n1
ID# ATTRIBUTE_NAME          FLAG     VALUE WORST THRESH TYPE      UPDATED  WHEN_FAILED RAW_VALUE
5 Reallocated_Sector_Ct     0x0033   100   100   036    Pre-fail  Always       -       4
177 Wear_Leveling_Count     0x0013   087   087   000    Pre-fail  Always       -       23
```
Seeing small upticks in reallocated count on a few drives. Also write amplification from scrubs is nontrivial.

olivia: Impact summary — GPU attach latency jumped x3, provisioning queue backed up; we temporarily routed a handful of requests to remote volumes to keep customers alive which increased I/O latency and added ~$1200 in egress + extra instance hours in the 02:00-03:00 window.

kai: Immediate mitigations applied:
- throttled janitor concurrency to 5% via controller patch
- rescheduled remaining scrub tasks to a night window (03:30 -> 07:00)
- rolled back node label automation and re-asserted `scratch-affinity=preferred`
- temporarily enabled model routing to dedicated capacity for high-SLA jobs
Commands run: 
```sh
kubectl patch deployment janitor-controller -n infra --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":1}]'
kubectl label nodes -l rollout=netcfg scratch-affinity=preferred --overwrite
```

mike: After the patch ive sampled iostat again on the same host, util dropped to ~12% and avgqu-sz < 0.5 within 6m. Reallocated counters not increasing further on that host. Keeping an eye on wear metrics.

oncall: Oncall will monitor the cluster for the next 6 hours and escalate if nvme error rates or attach timeouts reoccur. Alert thresholds adjusted: attach_timeout_rate > 5% for 5m -> page.

olivia: Thanks team — good catch. Follow ups: add a guard to the netcfg rollout automation so it doesn't remove scratch-affinity labels, add a pre-step to drain janitor scheduling before label churn, and add an alert linking scrub concurrency -> provisioning latency. Filing a follow-up doc/CR now. :thumbsup:
